source.title: Larne Times, 26 July 1930, p. 4 ("Tuberculosis medical officer (Antrim County Council quarterly meeting)"); Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1930, p. 7 ("Local elections in Ulster: no contests for seats on Antrim County Council; list of nominations"); Northern Whig, 5 May 1927, p. 8 ("Antrim County Council: nominations for the triennial elections; four contests likely"); Larne Times, 18 October 1930, p. 3 ("Obituary: respected Glenarm lady"); Ballymena Weekly Telegraph, 6 December 1930, p. 5 ("Glenarm farmers: milk association")

source.check: returned unopposed: no nomination was received for the division and the retiring member continued (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1930, p. 7); named as a sitting member of the new council early in the term (Larne Times, 26 July 1930, p. 4: Mr. Thomson explained the letting of the Albert Hall building as a school and spoke when the repair of schools was discussed; Larne Times, 18 October 1930, p. 3: 'John Thomson, J.P., Co.C.' among the mourners; Ballymena Weekly Telegraph, 6 December 1930, p. 5: the chair was taken by 'Mr. John Thomson, J.P., County Council[lor]')

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received by Andrew (Alexander) Millar, secretary, at the County Courthouse, Belfast, on 7 May 1930, and there were no contests in any division (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1930). No poll was therefore held: the statutory election day was Thursday 5 June 1930, the day fixed for the local elections that year (Belfast municipal polling '5th June', Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1930, p. 9; guardians election 'Thursday, 5th June', Irish News, 30 April 1930, p. 6). The queue's provisional 29 May is not supported by any source seen. The News-Letter prints no party labels and no sitting-member asterisks, so neither is given. Added from reports of the new council's meetings early in the term, each division inferred from the previous return: Dunminning, Kirkinriola and Glenarm. division inferred from the 2 June 1927 return (John Thompson, J.P.; Northern Whig, 5 May 1927, p. 8); the Larne Times, 26 July 1930, p. 4 names the member as sitting for the new council (quarterly meeting of Antrim County Council, County Courthouse, Crumlin Road, Belfast, July 1930 (Lieut.-Colonel John Patrick presiding)). The 1930 reports spell the name 'Thomson'; the 1927 nomination list prints 'John Thompson, J.P.' and the 1933 list 'John Thomson'. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
